content.text: Digital creators in Nigeria face a stark reality: platforms like Gumroad and Payhip, reliant on Stripe and PayPal, are inaccessible. This isn’t a temporary glitch—it’s a structural exclusion. Your ability to sell digital products hinges on [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-solutions-zimbabwean-digital-sellers-every-detail-you-3|payment]] processors that reject your country outright. The solution isn’t a workaround; it’s sovereign commerce [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-courses-pakistan-without-stripe-explained-digital-creators-5|COREMERCH guide to selling]]-design-assets-crypto-payments-5|The Full]]. This breakdown compares Gumroad, Payhip, and COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack, analyzing how each handles restricted access, payment processing, ownership, and automation. The goal: clarity on which architecture actually serves your needs—not as a victim, but as a creator who chooses better tools.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Gumroad payhip

Gumroad and Payhip are platform-as-a-service solutions. They host your products, handle payments, and manage delivery—all within their walled gardens. This works until your country is blocked. COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack is base-layer infrastructure. It deploys your store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, uses Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and NOWPayments for crypto transactions. You own every component. No platform locks you out. Gumroad and Payhip are rental models; COREMERCH is ownership architecture. One is convenience until it fails; the other is sovereignty by design.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Gumroad and Payhip rely on Stripe and PayPal for payments. If these processors exclude Nigeria, your store is dead. Their platforms cannot bypass this. COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack integrates NOWPayments, which accepts 300+ cryptocurrencies without KYC. Buyers pay in USDT, BTC, or SOL; you receive funds directly. No middlemen. No country restrictions. This isn’t a workaround—it’s a structural alternative. While Gumroad and Payhip wait for Stripe’s approval, COREMERCH’s stack operates on networks Stripe can’t control. The choice is clear: rent a platform that fails you or own infrastructure that doesn’t.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Gumroad charges 10% per sale; Payhip starts at 5%. Both add Stripe’s 2.9% + $0.30. Total: 12.9% to 7.9%. Payments take 2-7 days. COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack uses NOWPayments (0.5% fee). If a buyer pays $100 in USDT, you receive $99.50 instantly. No platform cut. No payout delays. Transaction fees on BSC or Solana are under $0.10. Real cost comparison: Gumroad/Payhip take $7.90 to $12.90 per $100 sale; COREMERCH takes $0.50. Speed: instant vs. days. The tradeoff: Gumroad/Payhip handle everything until they don’t. COREMERCH requires deployment but delivers permanent infrastructure.
Gumroad and Payhip fail where Stripe fails. COREMERCH doesn’t rely on Stripe.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Gumroad and Payhip own your store, data, and delivery process. They can suspend your account or change terms anytime. COREMERCH deploys your stack to your GitHub or Cloudflare account. You own the code, data, and delivery pipeline. Automation is built-in: Cloudflare Workers handle orders, Supabase stores them, and Google Drive or R2 delivers files. No manual intervention. No platform risk. Gumroad/Payhip offer convenience until they become liabilities. COREMERCH offers sovereignty from day one. The choice: rent convenience or own resilience.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you’re in a country Stripe supports, Gumroad or Payhip might suffice—until they don’t. For creators in Nigeria, Ghana, or Zimbabwe, these platforms are non-starters. COREMERCH’s Edge Commerce Stack is the only option that bypasses payment processor restrictions at the base layer. It’s not plug-and-play; it’s deploy-and-own. If you value sovereignty over temporary convenience, this is your architecture. At $197, it’s a one-time investment in infrastructure you control. No subscriptions. No platform risk. For creators locked out of Stripe, this isn’t an alternative—it’s the solution.

It uses NOWPayments for crypto transactions, bypassing geographic restrictions. You own the infrastructure, ensuring no platform can shut you down. While Gumroad and Payhip offer convenience, they fail where Stripe fails. COREMERCH provides sovereignty—a permanent solution, not a workaround.

Creators researching Stripe and PayPal alternatives consistently arrive at the same conclusion: the problem is not finding a single substitute payment processor — it is rebuilding the entire commerce stack on infrastructure that does not inherit the restrictions of the conventional financial system. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 is the complete deployment: Cloudflare Pages plus Workers plus Supabase plus NOWPayments, deployed in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff, 30-day support included. If you want to build it yourself, the Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents both Stack 01 and Stack 02 in complete detail with full source code. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Accept that no workaround inside conventional payment infrastructure is durable — platforms actively close gaps as they discover them. Create a NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as your starting point — these cover the widest range of buyers in restricted markets. Choose your stack: Stack 01 for a self-deployed free setup using GitHub Pages and Google Apps Script, Stack 02 for the Edge Stack deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours. Configure the NOWPayments webhook endpoint URL in your IPN settings pointing to your backend. Upload your product files to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Complete a real mainnet test transaction and confirm the full pipeline: webhook received, transaction verified on-chain, order logged, delivery email sent, download link working. Share your store URL only after the mainnet test passes cleanly.
